patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a CA inpatient action plan that pairs DRG-level authorization review with contract and payment review for the highest-growth acute hospital admissions.

CA ABD Non Dual contributes another about +$0.6M in the same acute hospital setting.

The business risk is that true site-of-care and provider performance may be obscured by incomplete facility attribution.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Without correcting facility mapping, the organization may misread whether ECU is driving avoidable utilization, higher prices, or both.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate ECU facility mapping first, then complete a provider-level review of acute admissions, reimbursement, and authorization handling for TANF Standard and TANF Foster Care.
patterns_data.validation_reason: A material share of the increase is in Not Mapped facility records for the same provider, which can distort site-of-care and provider performance conclusions.

ECU HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER also shows about +$0.6M in Not Mapped facility records on 9 admissions with about +$65.1K higher paid per admit.
NC TANF Foster Care contributes another about +$0.2M at ECU HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER with 14 more admissions and about +$17.3K paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: A small number of severe inpatient cases are generating outsized spend, and some of that spend sits in an UNATTRIBUTED segment. The cases include pneumonia with MCC, trauma, GI obstruction, wound debridement, stomach cancer surgery, and other severe one-off admissions. These do not indicate a broad trend, but they are large enough to require both attribution cleanup and case-level review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rare cases can materially distort trend narratives and may reveal gaps in attribution, case management, or escalation handling.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Have clinical and data-quality teams validate attribution and complete case-level review on the highest-cost admissions to separate one-time shocks from emerging severe-case patterns.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by small numbers of very high-cost cases and includes an UNATTRIBUTED segment, so attribution and case identification should be confirmed before broader action.
evidence_summary: UNATTRIBUTED severe cases total about +$0.8M, led by pneumonia with MCC at about +$0.4M on 5 admissions and trauma with MCC at about +$0.3M on 4 admissions.
IA / IN / OH rare cases add about +$0.3M, including about +$89K for a stomach procedure at IOWA METHODIST MEDICAL CENTER.
Multiple AMG SPECIALTY HOSPITAL CENTRAL INDIANA - MUNCIE cases are single-admission outliers ranging from about +$25K to +$42K.

patterns_data.pattern_details: IN Family Care spend is rising through a combination of more acute hospital admissions and higher-cost LTCH episodes tied to AMG SPECIALTY HOSPITAL CENTRAL INDIANA - MUNCIE. Acute hospital growth is mostly volume-driven in major bowel procedures, while LTCH adds a smaller but more expensive setting. The pattern suggests episode economics and transfer behavior deserve focused review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Episodes that extend into LTCH can materially increase spend even when acute paid per admit is stable or falling.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Complete a provider-level episode review for Family Care cases involving AMG and related acute stays to assess transfer patterns, medical necessity, and LTCH reimbursement terms.
evidence_summary: IN Family Care ACUTE HOSPITAL adds about +$0.4M in Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC with 17 more admissions.
